comment: Example MCP server configuration for GitHub Copilot in VS Code. Place this file at .vscode/mcp.json in your workspace, or configure via VS Code user settings.

github.comment: GitHub MCP server — gives Copilot access to issues, PRs, repos, and more via the GitHub API

postgres.comment: PostgreSQL MCP server — gives Copilot read access to database schema and the ability to run queries

sqlite.comment: SQLite MCP server — useful for local development databases

filesystem.comment: Filesystem MCP server — gives Copilot access to files outside the workspace (use with care)

brave-search.comment: Brave Search MCP server — gives Copilot the ability to search the web

notes.authentication: All MCP servers that call authenticated APIs require the relevant token set as an environment variable. Use a .env file (gitignored) or your shell profile.
notes.github_token: Generate a GitHub Personal Access Token at github.com/settings/tokens with 'repo' and 'issues' scopes, OR use: export GITHUB_TOKEN=$(gh auth token)
notes.security: MCP servers run as local processes with the permissions of your user account. Only configure MCP servers you trust. Never commit secrets or tokens to this file — use environment variable references (${env:VAR_NAME}) instead.
notes.documentation: Full MCP specification: https://modelcontextprotocol.io | VS Code MCP docs: https://code.visualstudio.com/docs/copilot/chat/mcp-servers | GitHub MCP server: https://github.com/github/github-mcp-server
popular_mcp_servers: @github/mcp-server — GitHub issues, PRs, repos, code search
